title: Mitotically heritable effects of BMAA on striatal neural stem cell proliferation and differentiation.
ehr_evidence: We used primary neuronal cell cultures and embryonic neural stem cells from rat striatum.
summary: In vitro study investigating the direct and mitotically heritable effects of the cyanobacterial neurotoxin BMAA on rat striatal neural stem cell proliferation, differentiation, and morphology.
key_findings: 250 µM BMAA reduced neural stem cell proliferation through apoptosis and G2/M arrest.
50-100 µM BMAA reduced differentiation into neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes.
BMAA-induced morphological alterations (reduced neurite length, processes, and branches) were mitotically heritable to daughter cells (D1 and D2).

P1 cells treated with 100 µM BMAA showed decreased neuron percentage (31.72% to 16.66%, p<0.001), astrocyte percentage (34.38% to 15.49%, p<0.01), and oligodendrocyte percentage (15.75% to 9.42%, p<0.05).
Glutamate antagonists MK-801 and MCPG completely protected against BMAA-induced decreases in cell viability, proliferation, and morphological alterations.
captured_features: differentiation markers (β III-tubulin, GFAP, Oligo4, nestin)
study_design: in vitro mechanistic cell culture study
population: embryonic rat striatal neural stem cells and primary neurons
limitations: extrapolation to human development requires caution
